issues.claim: Sending every message to every node, as a Redis backplane does, becomes a bottleneck at this scale.
issues.problem: This is inaccurate for the SignalR Redis backplane. It uses per-hub, per-group and per-user pub/sub channels. A server subscribes to a group or user channel only when it holds a matching connection. Only broadcasts such as Clients.All reach every server. The cited scale doc says nothing like this either. The excerpt only says the backplane forwards messages to other servers and that the app must scale with the number of clients. A candidate would learn the wrong backplane model.
issues.suggestedFix: Reword to: 'A shared backplane through which every server receives all broadcast traffic (for example Clients.All over Redis pub/sub) becomes a bottleneck at this scale; it also needs sticky sessions and scales with client count.' Make the same change in the RU text and in the matching trade-off wording.

issues.claim: The ASP.NET Core SignalR documentation explicitly warns that persistent connections consume server resources and can affect other apps on the same server.
issues.problem: The scale-doc excerpt is truncated and does not show this warning. The only related text is that without Azure SignalR Service the app 'uses many more connection resources than a web app without SignalR'. I could not confirm the claim that heavy SignalR use can affect other apps on the same server.
issues.suggestedFix: Soften to what the excerpt shows: 'Without a dedicated service, a SignalR app uses many more connection resources than a web app without SignalR, and must scale out by number of clients.' Drop 'explicitly warns' and the 'other apps on the same server' part unless the sentence is confirmed on the page. Apply the same change in RU.

issues.claim: it is billed by capacity units and messages, has per-instance limits
issues.problem: Neither excerpt shows the pricing model or per-instance connection limits. The statement depends on the tier, and the source pages do not cover it.
issues.suggestedFix: Make it tier-neutral, for example 'is billed per capacity unit (with message quotas by tier) and has per-instance connection limits, so very large scale needs several instances'. Add a pricing or limits link, or drop the billing detail.
